clue.text: Odd bits squandered in feckless stretches

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the next word are thrown away, leaving only the even ones

explanation.surface: Stray scraps are wasted during a careless, idle spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits squandered' drops the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of FECKLESS, keeping the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out something is to make it last longer, so ekes means stretches a supply.

clue.text: Watch tower over one that's charged, reportedly

indicators.note: in a down entry this places the tower above what follows

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle

indicators.note: signals that the next piece is replaced by a phrase that sounds like it when spoken

parts.note: an anion is a negatively charged ion

explanation.surface: Someone in a tower watches over a person who has been accused, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says ANION is heard as AN EYE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep an eye on something is an idiom for watching it carefully.

clue.text: Stun with shock: a Brontë daughter seen with Browning?

indicators.note: a shock jolts the letters of the word beside it into a new order

parts.note: Anne was the youngest of the three Brontë sisters

explanation.surface: A Brontë daughter is stunned to be seen in the company of the poet Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with shock' rearranges STUN into SUNT. Browning looks like the poet Robert or Elizabeth Barrett Browning, but it means getting brown in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tanned by the sun shows a browning of the skin, the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: Step into 'some money that'll plague you

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: pence are small sums of British money
a stile is a step for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Stepping into a sum of money that will bring you trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly epidemic, a plague that afflicts people.

clue.text: Anything but cross examination by the Bar?

definitions.text: Anything but cross examination by the Bar?

parts.words: Anything but cross examination by the Bar?
parts.note: reads like a courtroom cross-examination by barristers, but means a friendly, good-humoured quiz held at a pub's bar

explanation.definitionFit: A pub quiz is a trivia contest at a pub, so it is a light-hearted examination beside the bar.

clue.text: Flower that the KKK rejoiced to see

definitions.meaning: a white star-shaped flowering plant of the lily family

definitions.text: that the KKK rejoiced to see
definitions.meaning: the three Kings (KKK) of the Nativity rejoiced to see the star over the stable

explanation.walkthrough: KKK looks like the Ku Klux Klan, but it is three K's for the three Kings, the Magi.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi followed the star to Bethlehem, and the same name is given to a white-flowered bulb.

clue.text: Hint whale's stomach will have fish

indicators.note: the middle of the body, so only the inside of the whale's name is kept

parts.note: the minke is a species of whale
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A clue that a whale's belly will contain fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' strips the first and last letters off MINKE to leave INK.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suggestion or vague idea, a hint of something.

clue.text: Burns silent ladies before these hours?

definitions.text: Burns silent ladies before these hours?

parts.words: Burns silent ladies before these hours?
parts.note: Burns, Silent and Ladies' each go before the same word for the dark hours, giving a Scottish celebration, a carol and an evening for women

explanation.walkthrough: BURNS NIGHT celebrates the Scottish poet Robert Burns each January; Silent Night is a Christmas carol; a ladies' night is an evening out for women.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn, which each of the three clue words can come before.

clue.text: Support dead-headed plant

indicators.note: deadheading removes the head of a flower, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the teasel is a prickly plant with spiny flower heads

explanation.surface: Prop up a plant whose dead flowers have been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up a painting or board.

clue.text: Understanding one's dropped chess player, the first to get licked

parts.note: when the penny drops, someone suddenly understands
Black is one of the two sides in chess

explanation.surface: A chess player gets it once something falls, the first to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licked' suggests a beaten player, but it is a stamp being licked.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penny Black of 1840 was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, licked before sticking.

clue.text: Wherein soldiers enter, say, to find disembowelled guerrillas

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: with the insides removed, only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Soldiers move in to find guerrillas who have been gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, soldiers are thin strips of toast dipped into soft-boiled eggs, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast soldiers are dunked into boiled eggs, so the eggs are what the soldiers go into.

clue.text: Cross with university grabbing area where pleasure-dome was planned

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: one piece takes hold of another inside it

parts.note: with can mean and, as in fish with chips

explanation.surface: Angry at a university seizing a region where a pleasure-dome was proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts A inside AND+U.
explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan, Kubla Khan decreed a stately pleasure-dome in Xanadu.

clue.text: Poor relation from the East End?

indicators.note: something poorly made is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An impoverished family member from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a traditionally working-class part of London, but here the eastern end of the world, the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means belonging to the East, the Far East being the world's eastern end.

clue.text: The second one to be celebrated by paper

definitions.text: The second one to be celebrated by paper

parts.words: The second one to be celebrated by paper
parts.note: after the wedding day itself, the next marked occasion is the first year's, traditionally marked with paper gifts

explanation.definitionFit: The first wedding anniversary is the paper one, the second celebration after the wedding itself.

clue.text: She's reportedly in charge of make-up

indicators.note: signals that a word is replaced by another that sounds the same

parts.note: a gene controls part of a living thing's genetic make-up

explanation.surface: A woman who, so they say, runs the cosmetics department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but it is the genetic constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a woman's name, so it can stand for she.

clue.text: Sweet but ugly woman entertained by a man, almost unknown before

indicators.note: the unknown is placed in front of the rest

parts.note: z is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: a host entertains a guest inside, so one piece goes within the others
the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Lionel is a man's name
bag is slang for an unattractive woman

explanation.surface: A dessert, but an unattractive woman was entertained by a near-stranger before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the man's name; 'entertained by' sets the ugly woman inside A plus that shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian dessert of whipped egg yolks, sugar and wine.

clue.text: In which Letter from America might originally have been written?

definitions.text: In which Letter from America might originally have been written?

parts.words: In which Letter from America might originally have been written?
parts.note: Letter from America was Alistair Cooke's radio talk; here it is a letter written by America's original people, in a black drawing ink

explanation.walkthrough: Letter from America was a long-running BBC radio talk by Alistair Cooke; 'originally' points to Native Americans, once called Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian ink is a dense black ink used for drawing and lettering.

clue.text: Possible result of distention when exercising

definitions.text: Possible result of distention when exercising

indicators.note: letters exercised are worked about, so they come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Swelling during a workout could lead to an inflamed sinew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when exercising' rearranges the letters of DISTENTION; the whole clue also describes the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of a tendon is a common sports injury brought on by strain during exercise.

clue.text: Under collar, plant punch

indicators.note: in a down entry the plant goes beneath the collar

parts.note: to collar a criminal is to nail or arrest them
to set is to plant seeds or seedlings

explanation.surface: Under a garment's collar, a flower is punched in.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail set is a punch-like tool used to drive nail heads below a surface.

clue.text: Spice Girl's keeping very loud, so husband leaves

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it
a letter departs from the name

parts.note: Sharon is a girl's name
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl who is very noisy, so her husband walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes the husband's letter from the girl's name; 'keeping' then holds the very-loud marking inside it, giving SARON with FF inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a costly spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Enthusiastic backing for Callas, say

indicators.note: the word is read back to front

parts.note: avid means keen or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Keen support for the soprano Maria Callas.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was a famous operatic soprano, an example of a prima donna.

clue.text: Coriolanus refusing gold to revolt, not wanting to go with the crowd

definitions.text: not wanting to go with the crowd

indicators.note: letters in revolt rise up and turn about into a new order
the name turns away the precious metal, so those letters go

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Coriolanus spurns money to rebel, aloof from the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refusing' takes OR out of CORIOLANUS, leaving CIOLANUS, which 'to revolt' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsociable avoids company and prefers not to mix with others.

clue.text: Seize up —- it's almost certain to clog

indicators.note: a clog blocks a pipe from inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is left off

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Something locks up, almost certain to block it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SURE to SUR, which goes into UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize a throne or power wrongfully.

clue.text: Display of extreme emotion as partners court inside

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: South and North are partners at bridge
to court is to woo

explanation.surface: A dramatic show of feeling while a couple romance each other indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners, abbreviated N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A swoon is a faint, a dramatic response to overwhelming emotion.

clue.text: Put air conditioning into burning carriage

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a fire is a burning

explanation.surface: Fit air conditioning into a vehicle that is on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a small horse-drawn hackney carriage, originally Parisian.

clue.text: Immediately after getting voucher, business stopped

indicators.note: the firm is halted, so its letters are taken away

parts.note: a coupon is a voucher
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: As soon as a voucher arrived, the firm shut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Upon can mean straight after, as in 'upon arrival'.

clue.text: Foul old harpies not quite making the ball

indicators.note: something fouled up is muddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nasty old witches fail to get to the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball looks like a dance, but it is a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheroidal means shaped nearly like a sphere, almost but not quite a perfect globe.

clue.text: Flower stall with little time 'to check on

parts.note: a pen or stall holds animals
T is the abbreviation for time
to stem is to check or stop a flow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower stall pauses briefly to keep an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Penstemon is a garden plant with tubular blooms, a type of flower.

clue.text: Permissible to replace old It's A Knockout

indicators.note: re-placing means putting something back in a different position

parts.note: okay means permissible

explanation.surface: Allowed to swap in an old TV game show.
explanation.walkthrough: It's A Knockout was a British TV game show of comic team contests; 'to replace' moves the O of OKAY to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayo is the spelt-out form of KO, a boxing knockout.
